thread:
deploy-bot: pre-release check failed for release v1.42.0: env-parity: secret key index mismatch detected between staging and prod

deploy-bot: details: index 'auth/keys/0' exists in staging but prod has 'auth/keys/1' -> potential ordering-sensitive client expecting stable index. See diff: 
```
- staging: auth/keys: [public.pem, private.pem]
- prod:    auth/keys: [private.pem, public.pem]
```

nicole: wtf, ordering should be deterministic. Is this from sops/kms rotation or from our keystore migration?

raj: likely the keystore write ordering. We switched to map[string]string serialization in the migration which doesn't preserve insertion order. I flagged this in the migration PR but thought it was safe.

sam: deploy window is open (now +1h). Do we hold or rollback? How bad is the client break?

oncall-infra: client reads keys by numeric index, not by name. Some older services still use index 0 for primary key. Risk: 30% traffic could hit older services.

nicole: can we patch the keystore without a full rollback? Maybe reorder keys in prod to match staging while keeping same values (no secret rotation).

raj: manual reorder is risky but quick. Alternatively we can pin the release to v1.41.9 (rollback) and schedule a hotfix to correct keystore ordering + add canonical key name accessors.

sam: what's the time to rollback vs hotfix? Rollback = ~15m (releasebot unpin + revert), hotfix = ~40-60m (manual keystore ops + smoke).

nicole: we should prefer minimal blast radius. If rollback is 15m and hotfix 60m with manual ops risk, lean rollback. But check if any db migrations in v1.42 that block rollback.

raj: no DB migrations. Only runtime change to keystore client behavior in the new agent, but older agents are still in prod. Rollback seems safe.

oncall-infra: I'll prepare rollback steps and runbook. deploy-bot, please hold promotion.

deploy-bot: promotion paused by releasecoord (reason: keystore index parity mismatch).

sam: Nicole, Raj — can you create release notes entry for rollback explaining we will reintroduce v1.42 after keystore fix and include migration caution: do not rely on key index ordering.

nicole: on it. I'll also create a postmortem checklist item: add a keystore parity lint to deploy checks + add an alert when map-to-list serialization changes.

raj: I'll draft the hotfix branch and add tests to ensure deterministic key ordering (sort by key name before write).

oncall-infra: rollback window scheduled in 10m. Notifying product and support. 

sam: thumbs up. tagging @support to prepare rollback messaging. :thumbsup:

nicole: quick note for release notes: ACTION: Pin v1.41.9 -> releasebot unpin if rollback decision flips.

deploy-bot: to be explicit: current promotion blocked, release artifacts preserved at s3://releases/v1.42.0/; rollback template: `rb rollback --release v1.42.0 --target v1.41.9`

sam: thanks team. Keep this thread for final confirmation after rollback completes.

nicole: will update when rollback done.

raj: will push the keystore-ordering PR prep to draft.

oncall-infra: Rolling back now. I'll post status in 5m.

nicole: noted, updating release notes and support playbook.

deploy-bot: promotion still paused. change-window: 2026-03-15T17:00Z -> 2026-03-15T18:00Z (automated)

oncall-infra: rollback complete. Smoke tests green for 10m. Prod keys now match staging ordering. Closing lock.

sam: verified end-to-end on a few clients. Good job.

nicole: logging postmortem item; will schedule follow-up to prevent regressions. :white_check_mark:
